statements.impact_statement: The image replaces Debian's SQLite 3.46.1 with the official SQLite 3.54.1 amalgamation, verified against the published SHA3-256. Upstream fixed the FTS5 doclist merge overflow in 3.54.0. verify_sqlite.py checks the loaded version and exercises negative-rowid detail=none prefix queries in the final image. This version is packaged locally; Debian has not recorded a fixed distribution version yet.

This vulnerability is in the SQLite CLI .recover dot-command. build-sqlite.sh compiles only sqlite3.c into a shared library; shell.c is not compiled or installed. The final distroless image contains no SQLite CLI, and verify_sqlite.py checks the executable locations. The Python sqlite3 module and FTS5 remain available.

The image loads checksum-pinned upstream SQLite 3.54.1, which includes secure-delete bounds fix d9de6eedbe918c074c7556400fa21df5960704d9 from 3.54.0. Debian records the upstream fix at https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-119374. verify_sqlite.py deserializes the public-domain 5120-byte corrupted database from that exact upstream regression and requires DELETE to return SQLITE_CORRUPT without a crash. Package versions and architectures here are exact; trixie has no fixed distribution version.

The source-built shared library omits SQLITE_ENABLE_SESSION. verify_sqlite.py requires sqlite_compileoption_used(ENABLE_SESSION)=0 and absence of sqlite3changeset_apply and sqlite3session_create symbols in the actually loaded library. This prevents the vulnerable sessionUpdateFind changeset path from being present. Debian identifies that path at https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-119379. This statement covers only these exact CPU library packages; unrelated SQLite builds are not assessed.
